summary: Dormant or disabled person can read sensitive data. Why: Unused access to sensitive data is pure risk. Severity High (access.py:175).

name: Rule 8: Disabled user still holds roles
summary: Disabled user still holds roles. Why: Re-enabling the user brings all access back at once. Severity Low (access.py:175).

name: Rule 9: Privilege granted to PUBLIC
summary: Privilege granted to PUBLIC. Why: Every user, present and future, gets it. Severity High (access.py:176).

name: Rule 10: Person can write to a sensitive object
summary: Person can write to a sensitive object. Why: Writes to sensitive data should come from the build or a service user. Severity Medium (access.py:176).

name: Rule 11: Sensitive object reachable through a group role
summary: Sensitive object reachable through a group role. Why: Group membership is managed outside Snowflake, so reviews miss it. Severity Low (access.py:176).

name: Rule 12: Admin role is a user's default role
summary: Admin role is a user's default role. Why: Every session starts with admin rights. Severity High (access.py:176).

name: Rule 13: Orphan role: no users and no parent roles
summary: Orphan role: no users and no parent roles. Why: Unused roles hide access that nobody reviews. Severity Low (access.py:176).

name: Rule 14: f'Chain deeper than {MAX_DEPTH_RULE} roles'
summary: f'Chain deeper than {MAX_DEPTH_RULE} roles'. Why: Long chains are hard to review and hide where access comes from. Severity Low (access.py:176).

name: Rule 15: Future grant in a schema that holds sensitive data
summary: Future grant in a schema that holds sensitive data. Why: New tables there are readable before anyone classifies them. Severity Medium (access.py:176).

name: Rule 16: f'Dormant user (no login for {DORMANT_DAYS} days) still holds roles'
summary: f'Dormant user (no login for {DORMANT_DAYS} days) still holds roles'. Why: Unused accounts are an easy way in. Severity Medium (access.py:177).

name: Rule 17: Read-only role can write
summary: Read-only role can write. Why: The role name or its use says read-only, but it can change data. Severity High (access.py:177).

name: Rule 18: Unusual privilege set
summary: Unusual privilege set. Why: The role holds more or fewer privileges than its capability (READ, WRITE, ...) stands for, so its name no longer tells what it can do. Severity Low (access.py:177).

name: Rule 19: EXECUTE TASK held by a person or consumer role
summary: EXECUTE TASK held by a person or consumer role. Why: Running tasks belongs to the build or a service user. Severity Medium (access.py:177).

name: Rule 20: OPERATE on a task outside owner/build roles
summary: OPERATE on a task outside owner/build roles. Why: The task runs with its owner's privileges, so whoever can start or resume it borrows them. Severity High (access.py:177).

name: Rule 21: Warehouse MODIFY or OPERATE outside owner/build roles
summary: Warehouse MODIFY or OPERATE outside owner/build roles. Why: Resizing, suspending or resuming a warehouse changes cost and availability for everyone. Severity Medium (access.py:177).

name: Rule 22: Stream on sensitive table readable without the table
summary: Stream on sensitive table readable without the table. Why: A stream returns the table's changed rows, so it leaks data its reader cannot read in the table. Severity High (access.py:177).

name: Rule 23: CREATE privilege on a schema held by a read-only role
summary: CREATE privilege on a schema held by a read-only role. Why: A read-only role that can create objects can copy data or change the schema. Severity High (access.py:178).

name: Rule 24: Person changed data or a table's definition
summary: Person changed data or a table's definition. Why: Changes should come from the build or a pipeline's service user, so they are reviewed and repeatable. Severity Medium (access.py:178).

name: Rule 25: Service user used from an interactive client
summary: Service user used from an interactive client. Why: A person is typing queries with the service user's credentials: nobody can tell who did what. Severity High (access.py:178).

name: Rule 26: Admin role used to read or change data
summary: Admin role used to read or change data. Why: Admin roles bypass the role model; data work belongs to functional roles. Severity High (access.py:178).

name: Rule 27: f'First access to a table in the last {NEW_DAYS} days'
summary: f'First access to a table in the last {NEW_DAYS} days'. Why: New use of a table nobody expected is worth a look, most of all on sensitive data. Severity Low (access.py:178).

name: Rule 28: Unusual volume on a table
summary: Unusual volume on a table. Why: A day far above the usual can be an export, a runaway job or misuse. Severity Medium (access.py:178).

name: Rule 29: Streamlit app shows its owner's sensitive data to people who cannot read it
summary: Streamlit app shows its owner's sensitive data to people who cannot read it. Why: The app runs with its owner's rights, so everyone who can open it sees what the owner role reads, not what their own roles read. Severity High (access.py:178).
